title: Solvable algebraic groups, geometric unipotence, tori and represented fppf quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Use algebraic closures [def-weil-algebraic-closure], general linear group schemes [sk-d-geometry], flat morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented morphisms [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and $k$-group schemes and their homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], finite type morphisms [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and the standard multiplicative group [def-sc-gm-ga]. An affine algebraic group is an affine group scheme of finite type. Scalar extension to a field $K/k$ and tori are those of [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]: scalar extension is pullback along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with the pulled-back group operations, and a torus is a group scheme whose extension to an algebraic closure of $k$ is isomorphic as a group scheme to a split torus of some rank $d\geq0$ (the rank-zero split torus being the trivial group). A smooth affine algebraic group is unipotent if it has a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation (a closed immersion into $\mathrm{GL}_n$) in which every point over every algebraically closed extension field is a unipotent matrix: $(r(x)-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. An affine algebraic group is solvable if it has a finite series $G=G_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_n=1$ of closed subgroup schemes, with each successor normal in its predecessor and each quotient commutative. Equivalently the next subgroup contains, as a subgroup scheme, every commutator of its predecessor; test this on all commutative $k$-algebras. For a closed normal subgroup $i:U\to H$, a homomorphism $q:H\to Q$ represents the fppf quotient when it is flat, surjective and locally of finite presentation and $i$ identifies $U$ with its scheme-theoretic kernel. Its represented fppf sheaf is then the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto H(A)/U(A)$, for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras.
